title: Tomato Early Blight — Alternaria solani
text: Causal organism: Alternaria solani (fungus). Symptoms: Dark, concentric ring-like lesions ('bullseye') on lower, older leaves. Yellow halo may surround spots. Stems and fruits also affected. Favourable conditions: Warm (24–29°C), humid weather with wet foliage. Chemical control: Chlorothalonil (Bravo) 2.5 g/L, Mancozeb 2.5 g/L, Azoxystrobin (Amistar) 1 mL/L — spray every 7–10 days. Biological control: Trichoderma viride soil application. Cultural practices: Crop rotation (3 years), remove infected debris, avoid overhead irrigation, stake plants for airflow, use resistant varieties.

title: Tomato Late Blight — Phytophthora infestans
text: Causal organism: Phytophthora infestans (oomycete). Symptoms: Water-soaked, greyish-green lesions on leaves turning brown; white cottony sporulation on underside; rapid vine collapse. Favourable conditions: Cool (10–20°C), wet/foggy weather. Chemical control: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold), Cymoxanil 0.75 g/L, Copper hydroxide 2.5 g/L — spray at first sign. Cultural practices: Destroy infected plants immediately, plant certified seed, avoid planting near potato fields, hilling reduces tuber infection.

title: Tomato Bacterial Spot — Xanthomonas vesicatoria
text: Causal organism: Xanthomonas vesicatoria (bacterium). Symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots with yellow halos on leaves, stems, fruit. Spots turn dark brown with irregular margins. Favourable conditions: Warm (25–30°C), high humidity, rain splash. Chemical control: Copper bactericide (copper hydroxide 2 g/L), Streptomycin sulphate 0.5 g/L — spray every 7 days. Cultural practices: Use disease-free transplants, avoid overhead watering, do not work in wet crop, remove infected plants.

title: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot — Septoria lycopersici
text: Causal organism: Septoria lycopersici (fungus). Symptoms: Circular spots with dark borders and light grey centres, with tiny black dots (pycnidia) visible at centre. Begins on lower leaves. Chemical control: Chlorothalonil 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb 2.5 g/L, spray every 10 days. Cultural practices: Mulch to prevent soil splash, rotate crops, stake plants.

title: Potato Early Blight — Alternaria solani
text: Symptoms: Angular dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves. Defoliation reduces tuber yield. Chemical control: Mancozeb 2.5 g/L, Chlorothalonil 2.5 g/L, Azoxystrobin 1 mL/L — spray fortnightly. Cultural practices: Certified seed, crop rotation, balanced fertilisation, remove volunteer plants.

title: Potato Late Blight — Phytophthora infestans
text: Symptoms: Irregular water-soaked leaf lesions turning brown-black with pale border; white sporulation on underside; infected tubers show brown rot. Chemical control: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil), Dimethomorph 1 g/L — preventive sprays before epidemic. Cultural practices: Hilling, destroy culls, use resistant cultivars, harvest early in epidemic years.

title: Apple Scab — Venturia inaequalis
text: Symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit; infected fruit becomes scabby and cracked. Chemical control: Captan 2.5 g/L, Myclobutanil 0.5 mL/L, Lime sulfur (dormant) — apply pre-bloom through petal fall. Cultural practices: Rake and destroy fallen leaves, prune for airflow, plant resistant varieties (Gala, Fuji).

title: Apple Black Rot — Botryosphaeria obtusa
text: Symptoms: Circular 'frog-eye' leaf spots; fruit rot starting at calyx end; limb cankers with orange-red pycnidia. Chemical control: Captan, Ziram, Thiophanate-methyl — apply during infection periods. Cultural practices: Prune out dead wood, mummified fruit removal, avoid wounding bark.

title: Corn Common Rust — Puccinia sorghi
text: Symptoms: Small, brick-red, oval pustules (uredia) on both leaf surfaces. Severe infections cause yellowing and leaf death. Chemical control: Propiconazole (Tilt) 0.5 mL/L or Azoxystrobin 1 mL/L — apply at early rust detection. Cultural practices: Plant resistant hybrids, early planting dates, avoid excessive nitrogen.

title: Corn Gray Leaf Spot — Cercospora zeae-maydis
text: Symptoms: Rectangular tan/grey lesions between leaf veins. Lesions coalesce, causing premature drying. Chemical control: Trifloxystrobin + Propiconazole (Stratego), Pyraclostrobin (Headline) — apply at VT/R1 stage. Cultural practices: Crop rotation, tillage to bury residue, resistant hybrids.

title: Grape Black Rot — Guignardia bidwellii
text: Symptoms: Circular tan spots with dark borders on leaves; infected berries turn black and mummify. Chemical control: Mancozeb, Myclobutanil (Rally), Captan — apply from bud break through veraison. Cultural practices: Remove mummified berries, prune for airflow, weed-free rows to reduce humidity.

title: Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot — Xanthomonas campestris
text: Symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, stems, fruit; spots turn brown with yellow halo; fruit spots are raised then sunken. Chemical control: Copper hydroxide 2 g/L, Copper oxychloride — apply preventively every 5–7 days. Cultural practices: Disease-free transplants, crop rotation, avoid overhead irrigation, surface disinfection of tools.

title: Strawberry Leaf Scorch — Diplocarpon earlianum
text: Symptoms: Small irregular dark purple spots on leaves; spots coalesce causing leaf scorch appearance; severely affected leaves turn brown and die. Chemical control: Captan, Myclobutanil, Azoxystrobin — spray monthly. Cultural practices: Renovate beds after harvest, remove infected leaves, use resistant varieties.

title: General Crop Protection & IPM Principles
text: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) for plant diseases: 1. Prevention: Use certified, disease-free seed; practice crop rotation (2–3 yr). 2. Cultural control: Proper plant spacing, optimum irrigation, balanced nutrition. 3. Biological control: Trichoderma, Bacillus subtilis as soil/foliar treatments. 4. Chemical control: Apply registered fungicide/bactericide only when threshold exceeded. 5. Monitoring: Scout fields weekly; record disease incidence. 6. Resistance management: Rotate fungicide modes of action (FRAC groups) to delay resistance development.

title: Pesticide Safety & Application Guidelines
text: Safety: Wear PPE (gloves, goggles, respirator) during mixing/application. Calibrate sprayer to deliver correct volume per hectare. Pre-harvest interval (PHI): Follow label — typically 7–21 days for edible crops. Disposal: Triple-rinse containers; dispose via approved scheme. Environmental: Avoid spraying near water bodies or in high wind. Resistance: Alternate between fungicide groups; do not use same FRAC code more than 2 consecutive sprays.
